meta.topic: AML and sanctions controls in instant payments

problem:
Meridian Bank promises instant euro payments that complete within 10 seconds, but its compliance team knows that sanctions, AML and fraud checks can take longer than the rail allows. A payment to a newly added beneficiary, a payment with a name that partially matches a sanctions list, and a payment where the screening service is briefly unavailable all arrive on the same morning, and each one threatens the instant promise in a different way.

The tension is real and must not be resolved by cutting corners. The bank cannot bypass mandatory screening to meet a speed target, and it cannot hold every payment for manual review either, or the instant product stops being instant. Verification of Payee is mandatory for instant euro payments from 9 October 2025, so the beneficiary check is part of the synchronous flow as well.

The bank must design fast automated controls with escalation and auditability, so the great majority of payments clear automatically inside the limit, and the small number that need human judgement are held explicitly, with a clear reason and a service level.
solution:
Separate controls by what must be synchronous and what may be post event, and document that split with risk appetite and legal advice. Sanctions screening of the payer, the beneficiary and the payment details, plus Verification of Payee, must be synchronous for instant euro payments. Transaction monitoring, behavioural analysis and some AML pattern detection may run post event where legally and scheme permitted, provided the post event work has a service level and a defined action when it finds something.

Make the synchronous path fast by design. Use risk based orchestration so a low risk payment to a known beneficiary follows a short path, while a higher risk payment follows a longer path with more checks, and both paths share a single synchronous decision deadline. Run independent checks in parallel, cache reference data that is safe to cache, and give every screening service a hard timeout with an approved fail open or fail closed rule per control. A mandatory sanctions service that is unavailable must fail closed: the payment is held or rejected under the approved procedure, never released.

Treat a potential match as a controlled hold, not as a system error. The hold carries the match evidence, the fields that matched, the screening version and the analyst queue, and the customer sees a clear under review status with a realistic next update time. False positives are recorded and fed back into tuning, so the same benign name does not hold the next payment for the same reason without review.

Keep the audit trail complete. Every screening decision records the input data, the lists and versions used, the decision, the decision maker where human, the timestamp and the elapsed time. That evidence is what lets the bank prove to a regulator, an auditor or a customer that the control ran, that it ran on time, and that the outcome was the approved one.

decision.question: A Meridian Bank instant euro payment triggers a possible sanctions match. The 10 second execution limit is about to expire. The screening service cannot give a definitive clear or match within the window. What should the bank do?

options.label: A
options.detail: Hold the payment explicitly, tell the customer it is under review, route it to a compliance analyst with the match evidence, and record the decision and the deadline.

options.label: B
options.detail: Tell the customer the payment succeeded while the review continues.

options.label: C
options.detail: Release the payment to meet the 10 second limit and review it afterwards.

options.label: D
options.detail: Reject the payment immediately without recording a reason.

decisionRationale: Option A is correct because a possible sanctions match must be held for human judgement with a clear customer status, escalation and audit evidence. Option C is wrong because mandatory screening must never be bypassed to meet a speed target. Option D is wrong because a rejection without a recorded reason cannot be audited or explained. Option B is wrong because it misstates the payment status to the customer.

steps.title: Submits an instant euro payment to a beneficiary in the channel
Validates the instruction and assigns a risk tier based on customer, beneficiary and amount
Runs Verification of Payee and shows the verified beneficiary name for confirmation
Run sanctions, AML and fraud checks in parallel under a single decision deadline
Applies the risk based decision: clear, hold for review, or reject
Reviews a held payment with the match evidence and records a clear or reject decision
Submits a cleared payment to the instant clearing system
Confirms the outcome to the customer and starts post event monitoring where applicable

happy: The customer submits an instant euro payment, Verification of Payee confirms the beneficiary name, sanctions, AML and fraud checks all clear within the decision deadline, the payment is submitted to clearing, settlement completes within 10 seconds, and the customer sees a confirmed completion with the verified beneficiary name.

negative.title: Potential sanctions match
negative.detail: A name or detail partially matches a sanctions list. Hold the payment explicitly, route it to a compliance analyst with the match evidence, and record the analyst decision and timestamp.

negative.title: Screening service unavailable
negative.detail: A mandatory sanctions service does not respond. Apply the approved fail closed rule, hold or reject under the procedure, and alert operations and compliance about the outage.

negative.title: False positive
negative.detail: A benign beneficiary repeatedly triggers a low quality match. Record the false positive, feed it into screening tuning, and keep the analyst decision on file so the next payment is handled consistently.

negative.title: Changed beneficiary data
negative.detail: Beneficiary details change after screening has run. Re-run the affected checks on the new data before release, and do not rely on a screening result for data that has changed.

technical: Store the screening decision as structured data with the input fields, the list and version used, the match score and evidence, the decision, the decision maker and the timestamp, all linked by correlation ID. Give every screening call a hard timeout and a recorded fail open or fail closed outcome per control, and never allow a timeout to be treated silently as a pass. Version the risk rules and the screening configuration with effective dates, and record the version used for each payment. Keep the synchronous decision and the post event monitoring as separate records so an auditor can see what ran before settlement and what ran after. Protect the audit trail from alteration and retain it for the required period.

accounting: No ledger posting occurs until the required controls have passed; a held payment creates a reservation only where the product design requires it, and a rejected payment releases any reservation exactly once. A payment held for compliance review sits on a compliance worklist with an ageing service level, and the customer is told it is under review rather than shown a false completion. Post event monitoring findings that require action create a linked investigation case with its own accounting treatment, never by editing the original payment record. Compliance reports screening pass rates, hold rates, false positive rates, decision times and service availability as control effectiveness measures.

scenarios.then: the payment is held or rejected according to the approved procedure. the outage and the decision are recorded

scenarios.when: the decision deadline expires without a definitive clear

questions.question: What is the maximum execution time for an instant euro payment?
questions.explanation: Regulation (EU) 2024/886 sets a maximum execution time of 10 seconds.

questions.question: When is Verification of Payee mandatory for instant euro payments?
questions.explanation: Verification of Payee is mandatory for instant euro payments from 9 October 2025.

questions.question: What must happen when a mandatory sanctions service is unavailable and policy requires fail closed processing?
options: Release the payment to meet the time limit
Skip the check and review later
Tell the customer the payment succeeded
Hold or reject the payment under the approved procedure
questions.explanation: Fail closed means the payment is held or rejected, never released to meet the clock.

questions.question: What may run post event rather than synchronously?
options: Transaction monitoring and pattern detection where legally and scheme permitted
questions.explanation: Only work that is legally and scheme permitted may move to post event monitoring; mandatory screening and Verification of Payee stay synchronous.
